<description>
**Problem:** `getblockfrompeer` restores a pruned block's body without recreating its undo record. If startup verification reaches that block at level >2, it attempts to disconnect it and reports database corruption, preventing the node from restarting.

With ordinary pruning, reaching the restored block requires a deeper check than the default six blocks. The AssumeUTXO case can occur with the default checks.

**Fix:** Stop deep verification when a pruned node reaches missing undo data, using the existing result for unavailable history. The same allowance covers missing undo on AssumeUTXO snapshot chainstates, matching the existing treatment of unavailable snapshot history. Level 4 still reconnects the newer blocks that were disconnected. `verifychain` returns `false` to indicate incomplete verification, including when undo is missing at the snapshot base. Lower verification levels and corruption checks for undo records marked as present retain their existing behavior.

An AssumeUTXO restart can still hit a [separate block-index candidate assertion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36452#issuecomment-6464524112) after verification.

This came up during [pruned `txindex` review](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36002). The pending `pruneassumevalid` change also needs verification to handle missing undo correctly, so this fix is being split out to land first.
</description>
